head: 0063b97c03045e285e128fed76d72f82bca4095d
scope: Uncommitted four-path UI font reuse source, including new test module. STATUS changes excluded. Source-only; no tests/native/GPU/window/capture executed.

resolved_findings.detail: Bare mod rebind did not resolve the new tests/fonts/rebind.rs integration-test child. Root added explicit #[path = "fonts/rebind.rs"] during source review; exact final bytes above include repair.

assessment: prepare_rebind validates every requested UiNode and widget cap before choosing reuse. It matches the exact ordered font-ID chain; changed priority or missing assets uses separately validated Self::new and retains original owner on refusal.

Retained UiFonts sources and engine catalogs are privately owned immutable Arc data. No package reload or mutable-catalog path is added. Existing native host reconstruction retains separate font-content ownership.

Reuse changes private shaper/cache scratch only. Accepted ShapedText, paint, glyph handles and atlas are immutable retained owners; runtime/paint/input/generation publication remains after successful native consumer admission and commit. Candidate fonts publish only with accepted UI state.

Known-chain reuse cannot accumulate new engines; at most the original 32 remain. Unknown chains replace with separately bounded requested catalog, rather than unioning historic chains. Font byte, node, text, aggregate glyph/line and atlas checks remain in their existing paths.

Shape identity remains font engine plus text and all TextStyle fields (font size, line height, width, wrap); Unicode direction is derived from actual content. Layout and paint arithmetic, order, clipping, halo and routing logic are untouched.

New source controls compare retained/fresh multilingual glyphs, lines, size and missing clusters, retain old shaped Arc/content, exercise reordered fallback candidate and missing/invalid/oversized refusal. These are not executed qualification evidence yet.
recommendation: No blocking production source finding. Proceed with bounded CPU qualification including the repaired integration-test path. A real same-workload measurement is still needed before claiming reduced host spikes or display improvement.
limitations: No new CPU tests, compiler, window, GPU or timing process ran for this review.
Private shaping/cache scratch may change during a rejected candidate; accepted visual/UI state remains the transactional boundary.
Long-lived engines retain bounded earlier chains until a replacement or owner teardown; this is intentionally different scratch retention from rebuilding every UI generation.
